**Multiple Choice Questions**

1. **Calculation of AgBr Production:**
   To find the weight of AgNO₃ and NaBr required to produce 93.3 lb of AgBr, you first convert the weight to grams: \( 93.3 \text{ lb} \times 454 \text{ g/lb} = 42338.2 \text{ g} \).

   The balanced chemical equation is:
   \[
   \text{AgNO}_3 + \text{NaBr} \rightarrow \text{AgBr} + \text{NaNO}_3
   \]

   Molar masses:
   \[
   \text{AgNO}_3 = 169.87 \text{ g/mol}, \quad \text{NaBr} = 102.89 \text{ g/mol}, \quad \text{AgBr} = 187.77 \text{ g/mol}
   \]

   Moles of AgBr:
   \[
   \frac{42338.2 \text{ g}}{187.77 \text{ g/mol}} = 225.47 \text{ mol}
   \]

   Mass of AgNO₃:
   \[
   225.47 \text{ mol} \times 169.87 \text{ g/mol} = 38289.25 \text{ g} \approx 84.4 \text{ lbs (rounded)}
   \]

   Mass of NaBr:
   \[
   225.47 \text{ mol} \times 102.89 \text{ g/mol} = 23195.99 \text{ g} \approx 51.1 \text{ lbs (rounded)}
   \]

   Closest answer: **(c) 52.7 lbs of NaBr and 84.7 lbs of AgNO₃.**

2. **Effect of Doubling Buffer Solution on pH:**
   Doubling the volume of a buffer by adding water does not change the pH significantly because buffer pH is determined by the ratio of the concentrations of the acid to its conjugate base.
   
   Answer: **It has no significant effect on the pH.** (Choose the one most appropriately describing no change in pH)

   Only **(d) CBr₄** has a tetrahedral molecular geometry.

   Answer: **(d) No two electrons can have the same four quantum numbers.**

   \(e^x \approx 1 + x\) if \(x\) is small.
